subject: Request: consent log format, retention, and subprocessor evidence for marketing tags
messages:
From: Lina Harris <lina.harris@acme-marketing.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Marketing Security <security@acme-marketing.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Consent logs / subprocessor evidence for marketing tags

Hi Dylan,

Hope you’re well — we’re finalizing our vendor intake for the widget you installed on our marketing site and the InfoSec team asked for a few items before procurement completes:

- Example consent event log (schema + sample rows) showing timestamp, consent signal, cookie id (pseudonymized), and endpoint receiving the event
- Retention policy for consent signals and logs (how long do you store raw events vs aggregated metrics)
- List of subprocessors that touch telemetry/analytics (including any advertising or measurement partners) and whether transfers to third countries occur
- Confirmation whether server-side tag calls include any PII in query parameters or cookies

Can you send the sample log and a short statement we can attach to the third-party risk assessment? We’re on a tight renewals timeline and would appreciate it by EOD Wednesday if possible.

Thanks,
Lina Harris
Vendor Risk Manager
Acme Marketing
---
Attachment: request-checklist.pdf (attachment stub)

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lina Harris <lina.harris@acme-marketing.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consent logs / subprocessor evidence for marketing tags

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (security) and Marissa (support/solutions) to pull the artifacts. Quick answers up front:

- We will provide a pseudonymized CSV sample of consent events (no raw PII).
- Default retention: raw event payloads retained 30 days; de-identified event indices + aggregated metrics retained 13 months. We can offer retention contract language for up to 24 months on request.
- Subprocessors for telemetry: our telemetry pipeline runs through Redwood-owned collectors and two subprocessors for storage and metrics (CloudStore Inc. and MetricFlow Ltd.). Neither receives raw PII from marketing tags; only pseudonymized identifiers and consent state.
- Server-side tag calls should not include PII if you use the standard snippet — we’ll include the snippet audit and a small checklist to validate.

I’ll follow up with the sample CSV and a concise security statement by tomorrow.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0192
---
Attachment: none

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consent logs / subprocessor evidence for marketing tags

Adding more detail for Acme’s checklist — draft language they can attach to intake:

1) Data categories: consent_state (string), pseudonymous_id (hashed string), event_timestamp (ISO8601), source_domain (string), storage_endpoint (internal id). No raw names/emails are recorded by default.
2) Retention: raw request bodies persisted 30 days; hashed identifiers retained 13 months; aggregated metrics (daily rollups) retained 24 months.
3) Subprocessors: CloudStore Inc. (us-central region) — object storage for daily batches; MetricFlow Ltd. (eu-west region) — analytics compute. Both subprocessors are covered by contract clauses in our DPA; transfers use SCCs where applicable.
4) International transfers: limited to subprocessors listed above; where data crosses EEA boundaries we apply SCCs and encryption-in-transit at TLS1.3.

I attached a short sample CSV with 10 rows (pseudonymized). Also attaching a proposed one-paragraph statement that should satisfy vendor risk.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head, InfoSec Partnerships
---
Attachment: consent-event-sample.csv (CSV stub), security-statement-draft.txt (attachment stub)

From: Lina Harris <lina.harris@acme-marketing.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Marketing Security <security@acme-marketing.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consent logs / subprocessor evidence for marketing tags

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from the security team:

- Can you confirm the hash algorithm used for pseudonymous_id and whether salts are per-tenant? We need to ensure ids are not reversible and cannot be correlated across vendors.
- For the 30-day raw payload retention, is there a delete API or automated purge we can reference? Our legal wants the operational control documented.
- Please confirm MetricFlow Ltd. processes only aggregated metrics (no per-event detail) when hosted in eu-west. If there is any per-event export we need to review the contract addendum.

If you can send the hash details and the DPA page reference to the SCCs, we should be able to complete the intake and progress procurement.

-Lina
---
Attachment: security-questions.docx (attachment stub)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lina Harris <lina.harris@acme-marketing.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consent logs / subprocessor evidence for marketing tags

Hi Lina — thanks for the follow ups, quick responses below and links to artifacts: 

- Hashing: we use HMAC-SHA256 with a per-tenant secret managed in our KMS. The per-tenant secret is rotated on a 90-day schedule; salts are unique per-tenant and not shared across accounts. This means pseudonymous_ids cannot be reversed or correlated across tenants without access to the tenant key.

- Deletion/Purge: we expose an automated purge for raw payloads via our console (Customer > Data Controls > Purge Raw Events) and an API endpoint (POST /v1/customers/{id}/purge-raw-events) that triggers an immediate deletion job; default retention policy still applies unless customer requests earlier purge. We can include an audit log entry for purge events (timestamp + operator).

- MetricFlow data scope: MetricFlow Ltd. receives daily batch rollups only (aggregated counts and percent opt-in by cohort). No per-event exports are sent to MetricFlow for EU-hosted customers. If Acme requires, we can arrange a contractual addendum restricting MetricFlow exports to aggregated data only.

Artifacts attached and linked:
- Signed DPA excerpt (see attachment: DPA_redwood_acme_signed.pdf)
- Link: Consent mapping doc (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-consent-mapping) — includes sample CSV and schema definition.
- Security statement: security-statement-draft.txt (attached), includes SCC references: EU Commission Decision (SCCs) clause identifiers are included in the DPA excerpt.

We’re happy to set a 30-minute call with Ben if your team wants to walk the artifacts. Let us know a couple of times that work.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Customer Compliance
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: DPA_redwood_acme_signed.pdf (attachment stub), security-statement-draft.txt (attachment stub)
thread_summary: Vendor intake for Acme Marketing requesting consent event examples, retention policies, and subprocessor details. Redwood provided sample CSV, DPA excerpt, hashing/rotation details, purge API reference, and offered a follow-up call.
